privacyPolicy: Alias Buddy sends data only to the SimpleLogin API at app.simplelogin.io, or to the SimpleLogin server address you enter in the settings. It sends your API key with every request, and, to create or look up aliases and contacts, the addresses of the recipients you write to, the alias notes and the names of new aliases. It does not send message contents. Your API key, settings and a copy of your alias list are stored locally in Thunderbird. There is no analytics, tracking or third party.
reviewerNotes:
What it does: when the user sends as a SimpleLogin alias, it replaces the recipients with SimpleLogin reverse aliases (created through the SimpleLogin API), switches to the identity of the alias's mailbox and blocks the send if anything would reveal the user's real mailbox address.

How to test: a SimpleLogin account is needed for the full flow; a free account with an API key (Dashboard > API Keys) works for alias lookup and creation, reverse aliases need a paid plan. Without an API key the guard still blocks sending from addresses listed in the settings.

Permissions:
- compose, compose.send: reads and rewrites recipients and sender in compose.onBeforeSend, and blocks the send when it would reveal the real address.
- accountsRead, accountsIdentities: finds the identity of the alias's mailbox and creates a sender identity for an alias.
- messagesRead: reads the message being replied to, to find which alias it was sent to.
- addressBooks: keeps the reverse aliases in an address book of its own ("Alias Buddy"), so replies reuse them.
- storage: settings, the API key and a local copy of the alias list.
- clipboardWrite: the copy button for an alias on the alias overview page.
- notifications: tells the user why a message was not sent.
- https://app.simplelogin.io/*: the SimpleLogin API.
- optional *://*/*: requested at runtime only when the user enters the address of a self-hosted SimpleLogin server.

Experiment APIs: none. This store build leaves out the Experiment APIs of the full build (src/api), so it does not check calendar emails, and an identity it creates while a message is open can only be chosen after saving the message as a draft and opening it again.

Services contacted: only the SimpleLogin API, https://app.simplelogin.io by default, or the self-hosted server the user entered.

No bundled third-party libraries. All code is plain, unminified JavaScript. The package is built with `npm run build`, which zips the src folder without src/api and without experiment_apis in the manifest (dist/aliasbuddy-<version>-atn.xpi).
